items.title: Investigators Probe Seatbelt Use as Mississauga Teen Remains Hospitalized After Fatal Guelph-Area Crash
items.summary: Ontario Provincial Police say they are investigating whether a lack of seatbelts contributed to the fatal crash near Guelph that killed four teenagers over the weekend. According to the Peel District School Board, one current and two former students were among those who died when the car left Watson Road South, struck a guardrail and went into a ravine early Saturday. Police identified the dead as a 17-year-old girl from Mississauga, a 15-year-old girl from Milton and two 19-year-old men from Mississauga and Brampton. OPP said a 17-year-old girl from Mississauga remained in hospital with life-altering injuries, while a 16-year-old from Mississauga suffered non-life-threatening injuries. The school board said it is providing support to students, families and staff affected by the crash and extended condolences to the victims' families. The board said it would not comment further while the investigation continues.

items.title: Peel Public Health Issues Conditional Passes to Four Mississauga Food Businesses After Recent Inspections
items.summary: Peel Public Health says it issued conditional passes to four Mississauga food businesses following recent inspections. According to the health unit, the list includes Food World Plus, a newly opened multi-unit grocery store at 50 Matheson Blvd., along with Fuwa Fuwa Japanese Pancakes, Pure Punjabi Sweets & Restaurant and Lazeez Shawarma. Peel Public Health said inspectors checked two separate sections of Food World Plus, its deli and its food square area, both on Nov. 2. The health unit said its routine inspection program covers restaurants, bakeries, takeout spots, bars and other food-serving businesses across the region to ensure compliance with safety standards. A conditional pass means a business can keep operating while it corrects the violations inspectors identified. Peel Public Health did not specify in its public summary exactly which violations led to each business's conditional pass.

items.title: City Nears Finish Line on First-Ever Dredging of Flood-Control Marsh in Northwest Mississauga
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says the year-long dredging of Osprey Marsh, a stormwater pond in the city's northwest corner, is expected to wrap up next month. According to Ward 10 Councillor Sue McFadden, the project is the first dredging of the man-made marsh since it was built in the mid-1990s, and is meant to restore its ability to help prevent flooding in the Lisgar area. The city said preparation work began in September 2025 and dredging itself started in October 2025, with crews working by barge. McFadden said the pond is not expected to be fully drained, except for its northeast cell, where sediment will be dried before being trucked away. The city said several trail sections near the marsh were closed during the work to allow it to proceed safely. The project is part of Mississauga's broader stormwater management program focused on flood prevention in the area.

items.title: City Councillor Says Mississauga Has Exhausted Other Options Before Moving to Expropriate Two Port Credit Properties
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is moving to expropriate two houses on Peter Street in Port Credit after police, firefighters and bylaw officers made hundreds of visits to the properties over the past year and a half. According to Mississauga city councillor Stephen Dasko, the city has exhausted other options for dealing with ongoing complaints at the homes, which sit across from Riverside Public School and near the Mississauga Long Term Care Facility. Police told CP24 the incidents led to more than 50 arrests and numerous charges. One legal expert told CP24 that using expropriation law this way is somewhat novel, since it is more commonly applied to clear land for major infrastructure projects like subways. The properties are located at 34 and 36 Peter Street, in the area of Mississauga and Lakeshore roads. The city has not said when the expropriation process is expected to conclude.

items.title: New Lego Store Set to Open at Square One This Friday, Completing GTA Trifecta
items.summary: The Lego Group says its new store at Mississauga's Square One Shopping Centre opens Friday, Nov. 6. According to the company, the roughly 2,970-square-foot store sits on the second floor in Unit 2-212, between La Vie en Rose and Indochino. The Lego Group said the Square One location completes a trio of new Lego stores opened across the Greater Toronto Area this fall. A Lego store opened at Markham's CF Markville in September, followed by another at Toronto's CF Eaton Centre in October. The company confirmed the Square One store would open to shoppers Friday morning, marking the third Lego-branded retail location to open in the GTA within about two months.
